title: Knocked out my cold in a week!
passage: I started taking Zincora lozenges the morning my throat got scratchy, four a day as directed. By the following weekend I was completely back to normal. These things work. They taste a bit chalky and the tin is tiny for the price, but I'm keeping a pack in my bag from now on.
cue: By the following weekend I was completely back to normal. These things work.
explanation: Gail credits the lozenges because she recovered after taking them. But colds usually clear up within a week or so on their own, so getting better afterward doesn't show the lozenges did it.

whyNot.fal_anecdotal_evidence: Gail isn't using her story to override studies or data; her mistake is reading cause into the order of events.

passage: Five straight losses, so on Saturday I dug out my grandad's old green scarf and wore it to the match for the first time. Final score: 3-0, our best performance all year. That scarf turned our season around and it's coming to every game from now on. Harbor City, you can thank me later.
cue: That scarf turned our season around
explanation: Danny credits the scarf because the win came right after he wore it. One win following a new scarf is easily coincidence, and the team's form has far more likely causes.

whyNot.fal_false_cause: Danny isn't comparing many games with and without the scarf; he's reading cause into a single 'this, then that' sequence.

passage:
Nadia: We put the Thermalyn smart thermostat in at the start of November, and December's heating bill was the biggest we've ever had.
Owen: Ugh. Those things aren't cheap either.
Nadia: Exactly. It's obviously costing us money, so it's going back while we're still inside the return window.
explanation: Nadia blames the thermostat because the big bill came after installing it. December is usually much colder than the months before, so a higher bill would be expected with or without the new device.

whyNot.fal_false_cause: Nadia isn't comparing many homes with and without the device; she's going purely on the order of events in her own house.

source: Councillor Teodora Quintero · Eastbrook town hall
passage: In March we finished installing the new LED streetlights along Harbor Road. By the end of June, reported burglaries in the area were down by a third. The energy savings alone justify the project, and our maintenance crews love them. But that burglary number tells you the lights work, and I'll be asking council to fund LEDs across the entire east side.
cue: that burglary number tells you the lights work
explanation: Councillor Quintero credits the lights because burglaries fell after they went up. Crime numbers rise and fall between seasons and for many reasons, so a drop that follows the lights doesn't show they caused it.

whyNot.fal_false_cause: No comparison with similar streets is offered; the case rests entirely on the drop coming after the installation.

title: Larkfield Bank expands coaching after branch turnaround
passage: Larkfield Bank sent performance coaches to its ten lowest-scoring branches after a record-bad first quarter. By the second quarter, nine of the ten had improved their customer scores. Regional director Felipe Arancibia called it clear proof the coaching works, and the bank will roll it out to 40 more branches this fall.
cue: called it clear proof the coaching works
explanation: Arancibia credits coaching because improvement came after it. Branches picked for a record-bad quarter tend to drift back toward normal on their own, so a rebound was likely with or without coaches.

whyNot.fal_false_cause: There's no comparison group here; the bank infers cause simply because the improvement followed the coaching.

title: Caching change: great results
passage: Hi team, we added caching Tuesday night: saving copies of pages so they can load faster. Wednesday's average page load was 1.2 seconds, down from 2 seconds last week. Visitor numbers were lower since the spring sale ended Monday, so the servers had less work too. Still, I've told leadership the caching change cut load times by 40%. Great work, everyone!
cue: I've told leadership the caching change cut load times by 40%
explanation: Mei credits the whole speedup to caching because it came right after the change. Visitor numbers also dropped that week, so the faster pages may be partly or mostly due to less work for the servers.

whyNot.fal_cherry_picking: Mei mentions the lighter traffic herself rather than hiding it; her slip is crediting the change just because the speedup followed it.

passage: Update on my stomach cramps: they showed up after dinner most days for a month. My doctor suggested cutting dairy for three weeks, and they stopped. Then I added it back and they returned within two days. Cut it again, gone again. One coincidence I'd doubt, but on-off-on-off is pretty convincing. Getting tested for lactose intolerance next week.
cue: Then I added it back and they returned within two days
explanation: Rosa didn't stop at 'it got better after I quit dairy.' She brought dairy back and the cramps returned, then removed it again. That repeated on-and-off pattern is much stronger evidence than timing alone.

whyNot.fal_post_hoc: One improvement after a change would be weak, but symptoms that come and go with dairy across repeated switches point to a real link.

title: Root cause of Thursday's checkout errors
passage: Checkout errors started at 14:02, the minute version 2.3 went live. Timing alone wouldn't settle it, so we checked: removing the update at 14:40 stopped the errors immediately; putting it on a separate test site brought them back. The error records also point to its new address-checking code. We're confident 2.3 caused the problem and have a fix in review.
cue: putting it on a separate test site brought them back
explanation: Arjun treats timing as a lead, not proof. Removing the update stopped the errors, testing it again reproduced them, and the error records point to specific code. Blaming the update is well supported.

whyNot.fal_post_hoc: The release isn't blamed just for coming first; removing it fixed the errors, restoring it brought them back, and the logs show how.
